title: W5 comment claims 'byte-identical slices, live vs replay' but the fast-path event lands OUTSIDE every hashed tick slice in the live app
evidence: app/main.odin:358  `events_before := len(app.state.events)` (captured at the start of each step iteration); :367 `pp.step(&app.state, app.tick, {}, &cat) // edits land via the fast-path`; :381-385 the added comment `// (v2-sound W5: the fast-path PIPE_DRAWN event is appended at // INPUT time with tick = apply_tick = inp.tick + 1 — the NEXT // step's tick — so it lands inside that step's events_before // window here, exactly where the replay's command-loop // emission lands it: byte-identical slices, live vs replay.)`; :390 `h := pp.state_hash(&app.state, app.state.events[events_before:], &cat, context.temp_allocator)`; :452 `handle_input(&app)` (where commit_draw appends the event — AFTER the step loop/hash/consume). core/serialize.odin:435-436 `w_u32(&w, u32(len(tick_events)))` / `for e in tick_events {` — the tick slice is folded into the hash.
detail: handle_input (:452) runs after the frame's step/hash, so the appended event sits at an index below the NEXT step's events_before mark (:358) and is excluded from every [events_before:] slice; replay's command-loop emission lands inside its slice. Live per-tick sim_hash therefore diverges from the manifest at draw ticks.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment: the live fast-path event lands before the next events_before mark (never hashed; live stats hashes diverge from replay at draw ticks — diagnostics-only), instead of claiming byte-identical slices.
